svg.title: Diluting 75% H2SO4 at 330 K with water at 280 K on the H–x chart
svg.text: Diluting 75 % H₂SO₄ (330 K) with chilled water (280 K): when does cooling start?
H–x diagram for H₂SO₄/H₂O attached to the paper (isotherms 250, 300, 350 K), redrawn
mixture hotter than 330 K here (max ≈ 354 K)
Water at 280 K: on the x = 0 axis, 60 % of the way from the 250 K (−204) to the 300 K (≈ 0) curve: H ≈ −84 kJ/kg.
Acid: go up the 75 % line to the 330 K isotherm (between 300 K at −310 and 350 K at −206): H ≈ −248 kJ/kg.
Join the two points: every adiabatic mixture of them lies on this straight line (lever rule).
The line runs above 330 K at first and re-crosses the 330 K curve at x ≈ 37 %: 1 + W = 0.75/0.37, W ≈ 1.0 kg.
Points a, b, c and the dashed example line printed on the original chart are left out here.
Redrawn from the chart attached to the paper (digitized curves); in the exam read the printed chart — values may differ slightly.
